title: Misunderstood argument to bufnew()
description:
Updates:
- Misunderstood argument to `bufnew()` - it's not the initial size but the growth unit [#73,#75]

None of these are critical, and my PR #75 did not introduce a bug, but the code + comments may be misleading to future developers.

title: Fix #64: invalid 'n' argument in upload
description:
Fixes two problems with "transfer-encoding: chunked":
- When method="curl", chunked decode is already performed but no
  Content-Length is available (hence the "invalid 'n' arg" error)
- When method="internal", chunked decoding simply was not performed

title: pick arbitrary contentLength if not returned by server (fixes #64)
description:
Sometimes, the rpubs server doesn't return a content length. Since the n parameter can be an overestimate, it is safe to pick an arbitrary number here.

(see https://github.com/rstudio/markdown/issues/64)

title: Fixed .requiresMathJax() matching to code from the R syntax highligting script
description: Moved the .requiresMathJax() check before the inclusion of the "R syntax highlighter" script to avoid false positive pattern match to the highlighter code. Otherwise, when the highlighter script was included also  MathJax libraries were enabled regardless of whether math expressions were actually present in the document or not.

title: Fix/encode
description:
`markdownToHTML` did not care encoding, so in some environments `knit2html` is not available.
Even worse, if windows user has utf-8 encoded .md file, he/she need to convert it into native.enc by hand.
This fix includes:
- `markdownToHTML` accepts `encoding` option.
- If `markdownToHTML` function is called from `knit2html`, it detect the encoding in `knit2html`
- output of `markdownToHTML` is always utf-8 (in the case of file output), in accordance with the meta-tag of HTML.

Please find the inline comments for more technical details.

The updated version has been tested with success under 
- OS X Snow Leopard, locale = "ja_JP.UTF8"
  - encoding: utf8 and CP932
- Windows 7, locale = "Japanese_Japan.CP932"
  - encoding: utf8 and CP932

I'm very very very happy if this fix will be merged and published on CRAN soon.

kohske

title: now work with MBCS (tested on CP932) on windows.
description:
Under locale=Japanese_Japan.CP932 (windows default in Japan), `markdownToHTML` sometimes fails.
This is because the line, `sub(perl=TRUE)` marks `html` as `UTF-8` (see `Encoding(html)`), and next call of `sub(fixed=TRUE)` a few lines below fails due to invalid multibyte string.

I think this is quite a simply bug, because `fixed=TRUE` in other calls of `sub` with a literal pattern.
Even worse we cannot run `knitr::knit2html` due to this bug.
This is very very serious... 

I hope this will be merged and `markdown` will be updated on CRAN soon.
Thanks,

kohske

title: Option 'mathjax_embed' for downloading and embedding the MathJax script
description:
This is related to [Issue #22](https://github.com/rstudio/markdown/issues/22)

I've added a `.mathJax(url, embed)` function that makes it possible to download and insert the MathJax script into the HTML document rather than to link to it online.  The downloaded Javascript is cached through-out the session.  This should solve the problem of viewing the HTML document offline.  It makes it is possible to create self-contained HTML documents. (BTW, should there be a global argument/option "embed" that forces insertion of MathJax, base64-encoding of images and more?)

The new feature can be controlled by a new HTML option ''mathjax_embed', e.g.

```
options(markdown.HTML.options=c(markdownHTMLOptions(default=TRUE), "mathjax_embed"))
markdownToHTML('LoremIpsum.md')
```

I've prepared `.mathJax()` so one can use different URLs (http, https, or file), but it's not clear how to make it a user option, because `markdownHTMLOptions()` only supports "flags" and no values.

title: Add header option to markdownToHTML
description:
This adds a header option to markdownToHTML, analogous to pandocs
-H include header option, which inserts the text or file into the
HTML header rather than the body.  This is useful if you have
custom javascript you would like to include in your final HTML
for example.

I think it is useful to have in markdownToHTML rather than using the fragment.only option and appending the html yourself as you can pass this header option when using knit2html in the knitr package.
